messages:
maya: opening war room — multiple customers reporting 5xx/timeouts from hosted inference in us-west1, tickets rising. starting timeline capture.
sam: copying. what do metrics show (5xx%, p95, queue length)?
leon: observed gateway 5xx at ~6.8% across gw-usw1 for last 10m, p95 gateway->runtime jumped 110ms -> ~1.6s, model-pool-3 queue depth increased.
kia: support confirms bursty reports from lumen-data and scribble.ai, some see 401->retry->502 patterns.
ash: grabbing traces — seeing lots of `auth.verify` calls waiting on kms.sign rpc which is timing out at ~1s.
matt: note: payer-service v2 was deployed 1761120000 (token verifier change). could be related.
oncall: deploy-bot: deploy(payer-service:v2) completed 1761120000 by ci/cd
maya: if v2 introduced sync KMS calls we might be blocking gateway threads. propose short mitigations.
sam: mitigation plan: (A) flip payer-service fallback flag to use cached verification path (B) scale model-pool-3 +2 replicas (C) temporarily increase gateway worker pool (D) customer comms draft. agree?
leon: scaling +2 now for model-pool-3. initiated at 1761123600, nodes expected in ~2m.
kia: toggling flag to skip KMS synchronous verify to fallback cached path.
infra-bot: feature_flag(payer.skip_kms_sync)=true set by infra-admin at 1761123705
ash: after flag flip, KMS requests dropped ~80%, kms.sign queue cleared. gateway 5xx fell to ~1.4%. p95 latency back to ~180ms.
matt: I'll rollback payer-service:v2 to v1 while we triage to be safe.
infra-bot: deploy(payer-service:v1) rollback started 1761123802
support-bot: creating incident tracking tickets: INC-2025-241 linked to S-9123 (lumen-data) and S-9124 (scribble.ai)
maya: good. leon keep an eye on autoscale, revert when stable. kia prepare customer status update (post to status.redwood.ai plus direct org notes).
leon: autoscale metrics stable, drain extra nodes at 1761125400 if no regressions.
nash: repro steps for infra devs: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hosted/infer?model=gpt-base` then tail gw-usw1 logs and filter `auth.verify.kms.*`. you should see timeouts when kms is overloaded.
matt: sample log entry we captured: `[gw-usw1] 2025-03-04T14:05:12Z auth.verify.kms.timeout pid=42 trace=xyz request_id=...` also saw many blocked threads in gateway stack dumps uploaded to s3.
kia: stack dumps and traces uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/1761123333/trace-archive.tar.gz
sam: root cause hypothesis: v2 verifier added per-request synchronous KMS signing/validation without a cache or async path; when KMS latency increased the verifier blocked request threads, causing cascading retries and 502/504s at the gateway.
maya: action items (owners/due): short: keep feature flag off until patch (owner: ash, due: 1761127200); short: customer comms posted (owner: kia, due: 1761124100); med: add local token cache+TTL and fallback in payer-service (owner: matt, due: 1763723333); med: add circuit-breaker + fast-fail for kms path (owner: sam, due: 1763723333); long: rehearse token-verifier canary and create synthetic KMS latency tests (owner: kia, due: 1766323333).
nash: I'll run a small staging canary of v2 with caching behind a flag once code landed.
leon: monitoring suggestion: alert on `auth.verify.kms.latency > 400ms` sustained for 60s and on gateway worker queue depth > 50.
support-bot: status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2025-241 (drafted).
oncall: observed stabilization window >20m, lowering severity in incident tracker.
maya: wrapping up — I'll write the postmortem draft and include timeline, RCA, and customer guidance (retry/backoff recommendations). meeting invite for RCA writeup scheduled. thanks team. :heart:
